name: OpenEmu/OpenEmu
description: A modular multi-system retro video game emulator for macOS with a native UI, Metal rendering, and support for 30+ gaming platforms from Atari 2600 to PSP via plugin-based emulation cores.
score_rationale: The premier macOS retro emulation platform with 17.4k stars; downloaded over 10 million times with best-in-class native macOS UI.
summary: Premier macOS retro emulator supporting 30+ platforms with native UI

name: nesbox/TIC-80
description: A free and open-source fantasy computer for making, playing, and sharing tiny games with built-in code, sprite, map, and sound editors. Supports Lua, JavaScript, Python, Ruby, and other languages within a 240x136, 16-color retro environment.
score_rationale: The leading open-source fantasy console with 5.9k stars; a complete creative platform widely used for game jams and education.
summary: Open-source fantasy console with integrated editors for retro game dev

name: mgba-emu/mgba
description: A fast and accurate Game Boy Advance emulator that also supports Game Boy and Game Boy Color titles. Features save states, video recording, Lua scripting, and both Qt and SDL frontends.
score_rationale: The best-in-class GBA emulator with 6.9k stars, MPL-2.0 licensed, actively maintained through 2025 with strong accuracy and feature set.
summary: Best-in-class accurate GBA/Game Boy emulator with debugging tools

name: snes9xgit/snes9x
description: A portable Super Nintendo Entertainment System emulator available across Windows, Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and gaming consoles. Includes both a standalone emulator and a libretro core.
score_rationale: A long-standing SNES emulator with 3.1k stars that remains a widely used reference implementation and libretro core.
summary: Established SNES emulator with libretro core support

name: bsnes-emu/bsnes
description: A high-accuracy Super Nintendo emulator focused on cycle-level precision, with true Super Game Boy support, HD Mode 7 graphics, and low-level coprocessor emulation for all SNES chips.
score_rationale: The gold standard for SNES accuracy with 1.9k stars; invaluable for preservation and reference even though development paused in 2020.
summary: Gold standard cycle-accurate SNES emulator for preservation

name: drhelius/Gearboy
description: A cross-platform Game Boy and Game Boy Color emulator with high accuracy (passes Blargg's CPU tests), debugging tools including breakpoints and a just-in-time disassembler, available for Windows, macOS, Linux, BSD, and RetroArch.
score_rationale: Accurate Game Boy emulator with 1.1k stars, valuable for both gameplay and Game Boy homebrew development due to its debugging tools.
summary: Accurate Game Boy emulator with built-in debugging tools

name: Lameguy64/PSn00bSDK
description: A powerful open-source SDK for original PlayStation (PS1) homebrew development, providing a C/C++ toolchain and hardware abstraction libraries for GPU, GTE, CD-ROM, and MDEC operations.
score_rationale: The most capable open-source PS1 homebrew SDK with 1k stars; essential for developers creating new games for original PlayStation hardware.
summary: Essential open-source SDK for PS1 homebrew game development

name: LIKO-12/LIKO-12
description: An open-source fantasy computer built with LÖVE framework and Lua, featuring a DOS-like OS with visual editors for creating and sharing 192x128 pixel, 16-color retro games and programs.
score_rationale: Charming PICO-8 alternative with 1.2k stars, but archived in 2024 making it unsuitable for active projects.
summary: PICO-8 alternative with DOS-like OS for retro game creation

name: google-deepmind/mujoco
description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact: a general purpose physics simulator for robotics, biomechanics, graphics, and ML research. Maintained by Google DeepMind with C API, Python bindings, Unity integration, and soft body simulation support.
score_rationale: 12.5k-star DeepMind-maintained physics simulator widely used in robotics and ML research, actively maintained through 2026.
summary: DeepMind physics simulator for robotics, graphics, and ML research

name: PavelDoGreat/WebGL-Fluid-Simulation
description: GPU-powered Navier-Stokes fluid solver running in web browsers via WebGL, including mobile support. The most popular interactive fluid simulation demo with 16k+ stars and native app releases for iOS and Android.
score_rationale: 16.2k-star browser fluid simulation widely used as a demo/reference for real-time GPU fluid dynamics on the web.
summary: GPU-powered web-based Navier-Stokes fluid simulation demo

name: google/liquidfun
description: Google's 2D rigid-body and fluid simulation library extending Box2D with particle-based fluid and soft body simulation. Supports C++, Java, and JavaScript across Android, iOS, Windows, Mac, and Linux platforms.
score_rationale: 4.9k-star Google-authored fluid+physics library extending Box2D, significant reference for 2D game fluid simulation despite being archived.
summary: Google 2D fluid simulation extending Box2D with soft bodies

name: InteractiveComputerGraphics/SPlisHSPlasH
description: Open-source library for physics-based fluid simulation using Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH), implementing state-of-the-art pressure solvers with support for viscosity, surface tension, and vorticity effects in 2D and 3D.
score_rationale: 1.8k-star research-grade SPH fluid library actively maintained through 2025, implementing cutting-edge simulation methods.
summary: Research-grade SPH fluid simulation with cutting-edge solvers

name: InteractiveComputerGraphics/PositionBasedDynamics
description: Library for physically-based simulation of rigid bodies, deformable solids, cloth, and fluids using position-based and XPBD constraint methods. Prioritizes speed and stability for interactive applications with Python bindings.
score_rationale: 2.2k-star unified PBD simulation library covering cloth, soft body, rigid body, and fluids — the reference implementation for PBD methods.
summary: Unified PBD library for cloth, fluids, and rigid body simulation

name: doyubkim/fluid-engine-dev
description: Fluid simulation engine SDK for computer graphics applications supporting SPH, FLIP, PIC, and level-set methods, with both C++ and Python APIs. Companion code for the book 'Fluid Engine Development'.
score_rationale: 2.1k-star fluid simulation SDK accompanying a published textbook, covering multiple simulation methods for game/VFX developers.
summary: Fluid simulation SDK with textbook covering SPH, FLIP, PIC methods

name: CubbyFlow/CubbyFlow
description: Voxel-based fluid simulation engine for computer games based on the Jet framework, supporting SPH, smoke simulation, and level set solvers with C++ and Python APIs.
score_rationale: 291-star voxel-based fluid engine built for games with multiple simulation methods; niche but game-focused scope.
summary: Voxel-based fluid engine for games with multiple solvers

name: mmmovania/opencloth
description: Collection of source codes implementing cloth simulation algorithms in OpenGL, covering mass-spring systems, position-based dynamics, and implicit integration methods. Useful educational reference for cloth simulation techniques.
score_rationale: Multi-algorithm cloth simulation collection in OpenGL; good educational resource covering diverse cloth simulation approaches.
summary: Educational cloth simulation collection covering multiple algorithms

name: NVIDIAGameWorks/Flow
description: NVIDIA's sparse grid-based gaseous fluid simulation library for real-time interactive applications. Superseded by Flow 2 integrated into NVIDIA-Omniverse/PhysX, but the original provides a standalone reference implementation.
score_rationale: 215-star NVIDIA gas fluid library; historically notable but superseded by Flow 2 in the PhysX SDK and no longer standalone.
summary: NVIDIA gaseous fluid simulation library for real-time effects

name: mackron/miniaudio
description: Single-file C audio playback and capture library with no dependencies, supporting WAV, FLAC, and MP3 decoding, 3D spatialization, effects, and backends for all major platforms. The de-facto standard for lightweight C game audio.
score_rationale: Extremely widely adopted single-header C audio library with 6.5k stars, actively maintained through March 2026, and used as the audio backbone for raylib, Godot, and many indie engines.
summary: De facto standard single-header audio library for games

name: ValveSoftware/steam-audio
description: Valve's open-source spatial audio SDK providing HRTF-based binaural rendering, physics-based sound propagation, occlusion, and reverb with plugins for Unity, Unreal, FMOD, and Wwise.
score_rationale: Industry-grade spatial audio SDK from Valve with 2.8k stars, actively maintained through February 2026, Apache-2.0 licensed, and integrated into major engines and audio middleware.
summary: Valve spatial audio SDK with HRTF and physics-based propagation

name: kcat/openal-soft
description: Software implementation of the OpenAL 3D audio API providing distance attenuation, Doppler shift, directional emitters, environmental reverb via EFX, and cross-platform support as the standard open-source 3D audio API.
score_rationale: The canonical open-source implementation of the OpenAL standard with 2.6k stars, actively maintained through January 2026, and the go-to LGPL alternative to proprietary audio SDKs.
summary: Standard OpenAL software implementation for 3D game audio

name: jarikomppa/soloud
description: Free, easy, portable C/C++ audio engine for games featuring virtual voices, 3D audio, real-time DSP effects, speech synthesis, SID emulation, and bindings for Python, C#, Ruby, GameMaker, and more.
score_rationale: Popular and feature-rich portable audio engine for games with 2.1k stars, Zlib licensed, widely referenced as the best pure-OSS audio engine for indie game developers.
summary: Feature-rich portable audio engine with DSP effects and synthesis

name: libsdl-org/SDL_mixer
description: The official SDL audio mixer library supporting multi-channel mixing, decoding of WAV, FLAC, MP3, OGG, MIDI, MOD, and Opus formats, with DSP effects and positional audio for SDL-based games.
score_rationale: Essential audio companion to the SDL game library with 685 stars, actively maintained through March 2026 with a redesigned SDL3 API, and used in thousands of cross-platform game projects.
summary: Official SDL audio mixer with multi-format support

name: LabSound/LabSound
description: Graph-based C++ audio engine derived from WebKit's WebAudio implementation, providing a node-based DSP graph for games, visualizers, live coding environments, and audio applications.
score_rationale: Unique graph-based audio engine with 782 stars and BSD-2-Clause license, offering a Web Audio-style API for C++ projects, though development stalled in 2023.
summary: Graph-based audio engine with Web Audio-style API

name: raysan5/raudio
description: Simple, easy-to-use audio library built on top of miniaudio, supporting WAV, OGG, MP3, FLAC, MOD, and XM playback — originally the audio module of raylib.
score_rationale: Clean, minimal audio API with 247 stars from the raylib author, useful as a standalone library or as a reference for embedding miniaudio in a game engine.
summary: Minimal audio wrapper around miniaudio for games

name: james-e-kelly/sound-bakery
description: Open-source audio middleware tool with an authoring application and C/C++ API, targeting feature parity with commercial tools like Wwise and FMOD including asset management, sound selection, and real-time debugging.
score_rationale: Promising open-source FMOD/Wwise alternative in early development with only 5 stars but actively worked on through March 2025 — worth tracking for future maturity.
summary: Early-stage open-source audio middleware alternative to FMOD

name: heroiclabs/nakama
description: Scalable open-source game backend server providing multiplayer, matchmaking, leaderboards, chat, social features, and user authentication for games, written in Go with Python/Lua/TypeScript runtime support.
score_rationale: 12.4k stars, actively maintained through March 2026, the leading open-source game backend covering nearly every BaaS feature game developers need.
summary: Leading open-source game backend with multiplayer and BaaS features

name: colyseus/colyseus
description: An authoritative multiplayer framework for Node.js with real-time state synchronization, built-in matchmaking, room management, and SDKs for Unity, Defold, Haxe, and JavaScript clients.
score_rationale: 6.8k stars, MIT licensed, widely adopted Node.js multiplayer server framework with strong cross-engine SDK support.
summary: Node.js multiplayer framework with real-time state synchronization

name: googleforgames/agones
description: A Kubernetes-native library for hosting, running, and scaling dedicated game servers, providing custom resource definitions for fleets, autoscaling, and game server lifecycle management.
score_rationale: 6.7k stars, co-developed with Ubisoft and Google, the standard solution for Kubernetes-based dedicated game server orchestration.
summary: Kubernetes-native game server hosting and autoscaling platform

name: kbengine/kbengine
description: An open-source MMOG server engine with a C++ core and Python game logic layer, featuring distributed load balancing and integration with Unity3D, Unreal Engine, and HTML5 clients.
score_rationale: 5.7k stars, proven MMORPG-scale server engine though development slowed after 2021.
summary: MMORPG server engine with distributed load balancing

name: googleforgames/open-match
description: A flexible and scalable open-source matchmaking framework running on Kubernetes, enabling game developers to write custom match-making logic as microservices without managing infrastructure.
score_rationale: 3.4k stars, Google-backed production-ready matchmaking framework designed to be paired with dedicated game server orchestration.
summary: Kubernetes matchmaking framework for custom game logic
